title: A call on a `mixed` value that is not a closure ends the program with an internal error no `catch` sees.
text: `mixed $f = 'strlen'; $f($s);` compiles, because `mixed` is the one unchecked position, and under `nvs run` it ends the program with `FATAL: internal error: a `callable` argument carried tag 5 rather than an object`, inside a `try` that catches `Throwable`. `?callable $f = null; $f($s);` does the same with tag `0`. A number, an array and an object of an ordinary class behind a `mixed` are not checked. [`closure::closure_arity`], `closure_param_tags`, `closure_param_names` and `invoke_address` each answer [`Fault::fatal`] for a value that is not a closure, which is the right answer where the checker proved the value `callable` and the wrong one for a callee it never typed; which of them a compiled `$f(...)` reaches first is not checked. What the call should throw instead is not decided: `rule:types/callable-is-a-closure` says what satisfies `callable` and is silent about a call deferred to run time. The checker's half is closed, since a callee whose static type can never be a closure is `E0420`. The fix is owed to `tests/hostile/tools/agents/a-worked-session/03-values-that-are-not-functions-are-called.nvs`, which carries this record's marker.
